USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

distal radius — pattern 3

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

After a bicycle crash, a patient has a fracture through the dorsal rim of the distal radius. The carpus remains aligned with the separated rim fragment but is subluxed relative to the remaining radius. The injury enters the joint. Which distal radius fracture pattern is described?

  1. Smith fracture
  2. Barton fracture
  3. Chauffeur fracture
  4. Die-punch fracture
  5. Colles fracture
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Barton fracture

Barton fracture: An intra-articular rim shear fracture with associated radiocarpal subluxation or dislocation.

Understanding the options

Barton fracture
Barton fracture: An intra-articular rim shear fracture with associated radiocarpal subluxation or dislocation.
Chauffeur fracture
Chauffeur fracture describes an intra-articular fracture of the radial styloid. The case instead matches Barton fracture.
Die-punch fracture
Die-punch fracture describes an impacted depression of the distal radial lunate fossa. The case instead matches Barton fracture.
Colles fracture
Colles fracture describes an extra-articular distal radius fracture with dorsal displacement or angulation. The case instead matches Barton fracture.
Smith fracture
Smith fracture describes an extra-articular distal radius fracture with volar displacement or angulation. The case instead matches Barton fracture.
